label: Immense: a primitive predicate for being contained by no place and present to everything
definition: PRIMITIVE. Immense g: g is measured or contained by no place and is present to everything that is. After ST I q.8 (God is in all things as an agent is present to what it acts on, and in every place by giving it being). Counterexample: a body, which is contained by its place and absent from other places.
note: Explicitly identified primitive (Encode first). Open semantic obligation: typed accounts of place and of an agent's presence to its effect. Distinct from INFINITE_2 (quantitative or spatial infinity of extent): immensity here is not having infinite extent. The only constraint placed on it is the open bridge 'Whatever causes the being of everything else is immense'.
